messages.content: Help me initialize a plain text presentation for a result set controller named 'dataController' within a parent composite UI element 'compositeParent', ensuring that the text area is read-only and supports multi-line input, horizontal and vertical scrolling?

function.name: PlainTextPresentation_createPresentation
function.description: Initializes the plain text presentation for a result set controller within a given parent composite UI element, setting up a styled text area with appropriate properties and listeners. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

controller.description: The IResultSetController instance responsible for managing the result set. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

parent.description: The Composite UI element that will contain the plain text presentation. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.content:
Here’s how you can wire everything together using the helper you have.  
The `PlainTextPresentation_createPresentation` function takes two string arguments that represent the Java objects you want to pass in. In your case those objects are the result‑set controller (`dataController`) and the parent composite (`compositeParent`).  

```java
// 1. Call the helper – this will create the StyledText inside the composite,
//    set it to read‑only, enable multi‑line, and add both horizontal & vertical scroll bars.
PlainTextPresentation_createPresentation({
    controller: "dataController",   // the IResultSetController instance
    parent:    "compositeParent"    // the Composite that will host the text area
});
```

**What the helper does under the hood**

* Creates a `StyledText` widget inside `compositeParent`.  
* Configures the widget with:
  * `SWT.MULTI | SWT.READ_ONLY | SWT.V_SCROLL | SWT.H_SCROLL` – giving you a read‑only, multi‑line area that scrolls in both directions.  
* Adds a `ModifyListener` (or similar) so that when the underlying result set changes, the text area is refreshed automatically.  

**Quick sanity check**

After the call, you should see a read‑only text area inside `compositeParent`. If you resize the parent, the scroll bars will appear as needed. No further configuration is required unless you want to tweak fonts, colors, or other styling options.
